"For each item below, fetch its source and check that the recorded quote appears on the page and supports the item. A card item is a field of the plan in the producer's words, with the sources it cites: check each factual claim in it against those sources, and any value it carries against the page; what the plan will build, measure or predict needs no source, but a factual claim with no source is UNSUPPORTED. For a cost input, check that the page states the number for the setting given; whether it applies to this plan is not yours to judge. When the page states a different number for a num or rate item, give it as page_value. Decide only from the pages you fetch and the text below; do not read files. Return one status per item, under its ref: SUPPORTED, PARTIAL, UNSUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED or UNREACHABLE, with the page sentence you relied on.
Items, one per line:
p1:step: ECMWF — AIFS ENS (operational machine-learned ensemble) has this step in its pipeline: Generating exchangeable ensemble members from one afCRPS/multi-scale-trained distribution and verifying them (including top-percentile events) to set the operational ensemble size. Today ECMWF draws 51 members (50 perturbed + control) and scores 50-member ensembles against IFS, flagging extreme-event skill as still-unassessed. | source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.15832 | recorded quote: \"The trained model is stochastic and can generate as many exchangeable members as desired and computationally feasible in inference.\"
p1:activity: AIFS ENS has been operational since 1 July 2025 and was upgraded from v1 (afCRPS) to v2 on 12 May 2026, alongside IFS Cycle 50r1. | source: https://www.ecmwf.int/en/forecasts/datasets/aifs-machine-learning-data | recorded quote: \"The ensemble model has been running operationally since 1 July 2025 and was upgraded from AIFS ENS v1 to AIFS ENS v2 on 12 May 2026.\"
p1:c1: Operational AIFS ENS runs 51 members on the N320 (~31 km) grid, 15-day, 6-hourly, four times per day; it is trained on 32 GH200 GPUs via the Anemoi framework by ECMWF's AIFS team (Lang, Leutbecher, Clare, Chantry, et al.). | source: https://huggingface.co/ecmwf/aifs-ens-2.0 | recorded quote: \"It is run operationally by ECMWF, generating a 51-member 15-day (6-hourly) global forecast four times per day.\"
p1:c2: ECMWF verifies AIFS-CRPS as 50-member ensembles against the 50-member physics-based IFS ensemble, using analysis and radiosonde/SYNOP observations — the same 50-member baseline the card proposes to exceed. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s44387-026-00073-7 | recorded quote: \"We compare 50-member 15-day AIFS-CRPS ensemble forecasts with the 9-km 50-member ECMWF IFS (Integrated Forecasting System) ensemble forecasts.\"
p1:c3: ECMWF has explicitly not yet assessed AIFS-CRPS skill for extreme events, noting CRPS's limited sensitivity to distribution tails — exactly the gap the card's top-percentile scoring targets. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s44387-026-00073-7 | recorded quote: \"An important next step is the assessment of the forecast skill of extreme events. Here, CRPS can have limited sensitivity to tail properties of distributions.\"
p1:c4: The card's 'check first' reproduction target comes from ECMWF's own reported N320 member runtime: about 4 minutes for a 15-day member on an A100 40 GB GPU. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s44387-026-00073-7 | recorded quote: \"a single member 15 day forecast is created in about one minute for AIFS-CRPS O96 and four minutes for AIFS-CRPS N320 on an NVIDIA A100 40 GB GPU, including the time spent reading the initial state and writing the forecast to disk.\"
p1:done: ECMWF has studied ensemble-size convergence for the physics-based IFS ensemble (up to 200 members, Leutbecher 2017) but has not run a 10–1,000-member AIFS-ENS exchangeable-member rare-extreme saturation study; its own paper lists extreme-event skill as a next step. | source: https://www.ecmwf.int/sites/default/files/elibrary/2017/17621-ensemble-size-how-suboptimal-less-infinity.pdf | recorded quote: \"50 and 200 members are 2% and 0.5% worse than ∞ , respectively\"
p2:step: HENS (Huge ENSembles) — NVIDIA Earth-2 / SFNO huge-ensemble project has this step in its pipeline: Generating very large ensembles and sampling their tails for extreme-event statistics. Today HENS builds members from bred-vector initial-condition perturbations plus 29 independently trained SFNO checkpoints (real model uncertainty), not from exchangeable draws of a single distribution, and measures information gain vs member count. | source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/earth2studio/tree/main/recipes/hens | recorded quote: \"HENS uses customized bred vectors for initial condition perturbations and multiple independently trained model checkpoints to represent model uncertainty, specifically designed for better representation of extreme weather events.\"
p2:activity: The HENS recipe is maintained on the main branch of NVIDIA Earth2Studio, which released v0.19.0 on 30 September 2026. | source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/earth2studio/releases/tag/0.19.0 | recorded quote: \"Earth2Studio general release 0.19.0\"
p2:c1: HENS (Mahesh et al., NVIDIA with LBNL, UC Berkeley, Colorado State, UC Irvine, PNNL) ran 7,424 members per day over 92 summer-2023 dates — the card's 'closest prior' scale, but with a different ensemble scheme. | source: https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/18/5605/2025/ | recorded quote: \"Here in Part 2, we generate a huge ensemble (HENS), with 7424 members initialized each day of summer 2023.\"
p2:c2: Their member-generation step is 256 bred-vector initial-condition perturbations per each of 29 independently trained checkpoints — the expensive multi-checkpoint machinery the card would test against cheap exchangeable draws. | source: https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/18/5605/2025/ | recorded quote: \"Here, we combine these two perturbation techniques to create a 7424-member ensemble: 256 initial condition perturbations for each of the 29 SFNO checkpoints.\"
p2:c3: HENS already measured tail-sampling (information gain ~4, i.e. 4-sigma events) as a function of ensemble size, showing bigger ensembles sharpen tails — but only for SFNO-BVMC, not for exchangeable draws. | source: https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/18/5605/2025/ | recorded quote: \"The 7424-member ensemble has an information gain of 4. This means that HENS is large enough to have at least one ensemble member that is 4 standard deviations away from the ensemble mean (on average).\"
p2:done: HENS already ran the 'more members sample the tails' experiment, but with SFNO-BVMC (bred vectors + 29 checkpoints); it does not test whether a single afCRPS-trained distribution's exchangeable members saturate, which is the card's question. | source: https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/18/5605/2025/ | recorded quote: \"We use this estimate of 7000 to guide our choice of ensemble size for HENS.\"
p3:step: Anemoi — ECMWF open-source ML weather framework (co-developed with European national meteorological services) has this step in its pipeline: Running AIFS-ENS ensemble inference (reproducing the member runtime/memory the card checks first) and evaluating the forecasts — the framework and its verification tooling through which the card's 10–1,000-member sweep and scoring would be executed and documented. | source: https://github.com/ecmwf/anemoi | recorded quote: \"As an 'end to end' framework, it provides a comprehensive toolkit that spans data preparation, model training, and inference, enabling meteorological organizations to leverage their own data for ML-based weather prediction.\"
p3:activity: anemoi-core is under active development, publishing graphs v0.9.8 and training-0.17.1 on 1 October 2026; the anemoi-inference package was last pushed 16 October 2026. | source: https://github.com/ecmwf/anemoi-core/releases/tag/graphs-0.9.8 | recorded quote: \"graphs: v0.9.8\"
p3:c1: AIFS ENS is run through Anemoi's inference package (anemoi-inference), which is what the card's 'check first' step uses to reproduce the published 4-minute N320 member time and 38 GB memory on external hardware. | source: https://huggingface.co/ecmwf/aifs-ens-2.0 | recorded quote: \"AIFS ENS v2 is implemented using the Anemoi framework. Anemoi consists of open source components, enabling the user community to run AIFS themselves.\"
p3:c2: Anemoi's verification is served by evaluation pipelines (e.g., MeteoSwiss's evalml) that run standard and diagnostic verification for Anemoi-built models — the tooling that would score the card's top-percentile wind/temperature/rain probabilities. | source: https://github.com/MeteoSwiss/evalml | recorded quote: \"Run evaluation pipelines for data-driven weather models built with Anemoi.\"
p3:c3: anemoi-training recently added ensemble 'graph scores' (energy/CRPS/variogram) for spatial ensemble scoring, showing active work on ensemble-verification tooling adjacent to the card. | source: https://github.com/ecmwf/anemoi-core/commit/11e8498e4b3fa38c32e80089f521387f7d2f19ec | recorded quote: \"These ensemble scores assess spatial structure across graph neighbourhoods, edge differences, global fields, variables (global energy) and spectral amplitudes\"
p3:done: Anemoi is a framework and tooling project, not an ensemble-size research programme; neither it nor its evaluation tooling has published a 10–1,000-member AIFS-ENS extreme-tail saturation experiment. | source: https://github.com/ecmwf/anemoi | recorded quote: \"The `anemoi` repository aims, for now, to provide a centralized overview of the entire framework.\"

function.name: webfetch
function.description:
- Fetches content from a specified URL
- Takes a URL and optional format as input
- Fetches the URL content, converts to requested format (markdown by default)
- Returns the content in the specified format
- Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content

Usage notes:
  - IMPORTANT: if another tool is present that offers better web fetching capabilities, is more targeted to the task, or has fewer restrictions, prefer using that tool instead of this one.
  - The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
  - HTTP URLs will be automatically upgraded to HTTPS
  - Format options: "markdown" (default), "text", or "html"
  - This tool is read-only and does not modify any files
  - Results may be summarized if the content is very large

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

format.description: The format to return the content in (text, markdown, or html). Defaults to markdown.

function.name: websearch
function.description:
- Search the web using the session's web search provider - performs real-time web searches and can scrape content from specific URLs
- Provides up-to-date information for current events and recent data
- Supports configurable result counts and returns the content from the most relevant websites
- Use this tool for accessing information beyond knowledge cutoff
- Searches are performed automatically within a single API call

Usage notes:
  - Supports live crawling modes when available: 'fallback' (backup if cached unavailable) or 'preferred' (prioritize live crawling)
  - Search types when available: 'auto' (balanced), 'fast' (quick results), 'deep' (comprehensive search)
  - Configurable context length for optimal LLM integration
  - Domain filtering and advanced search options available

The current year is 2026. You MUST use this year when searching for recent information or current events
- Example: If the current year is 2026 and the user asks for "latest AI news", search for "AI news 2026", NOT "AI news 2025"

numResults.description: Number of search results to return (default: 8)

livecrawl.description: Live crawl mode - 'fallback': use live crawling as backup if cached content unavailable, 'preferred': prioritize live crawling (default: 'fallback')

type.description: Search type - 'auto': balanced search (default), 'fast': quick results, 'deep': comprehensive search

contextMaxCharacters.description: Maximum characters for context string optimized for LLMs (default: 10000)
